title: Discovering Opinion Intervals from Conflicts in Signed Graphs

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph beginning 'Second, we show that BEST INTERVAL APPROXIMATION is NP-hard...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states, 'We show that BEST INTERVAL APPROXIMATION is NP-hard even when the graph G^+ ... forms a cycle.' However, in Section 2.1 the authors present a 'Revised' Theorem 2.2 that admits the reduction does not guarantee equivalence and the NP-hardness claim remains open. The claimed result is therefore not established, making the introductory statement false and misleading.

The text lists implications of the theorem: '(1) The disagreement version is hard to approximate within any factor. (2) It is not FPT when parameterized by the number of required edge deletions ... (3) The result holds even when restricted to graphs ... where G+ is a chordless cycle.' These implications depend on the claimed NP-hardness reduction, which the authors themselves acknowledge is invalid. Presenting them as consequences of the theorem is therefore unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, later paragraph starting 'This implies that (unless P = NP)...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'This implies that (unless P = NP) for BEST INTERVAL APPROXIMATION there is no FPT algorithm that is parameterized by the number of required edge removals, and that the disagreement version ... cannot be approximated within any multiplicative factor.' This conclusion is derived from the unproven NP-hardness claim and is therefore not justified.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.2, paragraphs beginning 'We attempt to solve...' and the immediate surrounding text
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 2.3 claims a PTAS for BEST INTERVAL APPROXIMATION with k intervals on complete graphs, independent of overlap structure (since all overlap patterns are enumerated). However, the text states, 'Due to these challenges, while a PTAS is feasible for limited and well-structured interval overlaps, the general case requires further algorithmic innovations beyond current methods.' This contradicts the theorem's claim that the PTAS works for any fixed k intervals and indicates an internal inconsistency in the presentation of the result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Introduction vs. Section 2.2 and Theorem 2.3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract says, 'comprehensive theoretical guarantees remain an open challenge.' Yet the paper presents Theorem 2.3, a (1+ε)-approximation PTAS for the problem on complete graphs, which is a substantial theoretical guarantee. The abstract's claim conflicts with the existence of this result, creating an inconsistency.

The caption states: 'interval 3 contains politicians from SPD, GRÜNE, and LINKE.' However, Figure 8 (which displays the same solution) shows that interval 3 contains no SPD members (0 SPD), only GRÜNE and LINKE. The description in the caption is therefore factually inconsistent with the authors' own presented data.
